# cc900 C near-miss index (generated by `scripts/analysis/cc900/nearmiss.py`)

QUESTION ANSWERED: for every function of our firmware C that Toshiba cc900 V4.23 compiled in the oracle runs below, how close does V4.23's code (translated by `model/to_llvm.py`, assembled by llvm-mc) come to the ROM, and which kinds of difference keep it from matching?  `index.tsv` has one row per attempt (run, option set, C file, function); the tables below take each function's best attempt.  No Toshiba text is in this directory: names, counts, offsets, class names and paths only.  The listings stay in the private repository `~/compartilhado/cc900-oracle` (`listing` column, relative to it).

Regenerate: `python3 -B scripts/analysis/cc900/nearmiss.py --src-root SRC --model-root MODEL` (this index: `--src-root ~/compartilhado/disasm-lanes/nearmiss (cc900/nearmiss@79eff2c76) --model-root ~/compartilhado/disasm-lanes/nearmiss (cc900/nearmiss@79eff2c76)`, near threshold 70.0 %).  Re-check after a translator change, without the VM: `python3 -B scripts/analysis/cc900/nearmiss.py --recheck [--class CLASS] [--all]`.  The classes and the ROM-size rule are defined in the script's docstring.

## Totals

| what                     | MATCH | NEAR | DIFF  | errors |
|--------------------------|-------|------|-------|--------|
| attempts (index rows)    | 19624 | 7048 | 10665 | 1592   |
| functions (best attempt) | 3607  | 468  | 225   | 310    |

Errors: ERR-asm 483, ERR-data 74, ERR-dup 70, ERR-name 381, ERR-resolve 360, ERR-translate 224 attempts (ERR-name: the listing's function is not a label of the tree; ERR-resolve: a name without a value or declared width; ERR-translate: a line to_llvm does not know; ERR-asm: llvm-mc refuses the translation; ERR-data: an f_const object (switch table, FP constant) without a `cc900-data:` line; the `why` column has the reason).

## What each class needs

| class        | needs                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| call-form    | a translator rule: asm900 relaxes `cal` / `j` to calr / jr / jrl when the target is in reach (to_llvm writes call / jp); lane_vmb's call relaxation should recover these without new C            |
| width        | a declaration: give the object the qualifier of the ROM's width (__tiny 8-bit, __near 16-bit, plain 24-bit), one declaration per name                                                             |
| register     | C idiom (temporaries, argument order, types) or an option set (-O level, -XS); rarely the translator                                                                                              |
| operand      | C: a wrong constant, struct offset or object; check the declaration's address and the member offsets                                                                                              |
| extend       | C types: an unsigned / signed char or int where the ROM promotes (or does not); a cast or the argument's declared type                                                                            |
| order        | C statement order, or an option set (-O level changes scheduling)                                                                                                                                 |
| loop-shape   | an option set (-O3 copies the loop test to the entry, -Xr without -O does not) or the loop's C form (for / while / do-while, the counter's type for djnz)                                         |
| swap         | C: the comparison written the other way round (`a == b` / `b == a`, `<` / `>`), which picks `cp r, (mem)` or `cp (mem), r`; if the C cannot express it, check to_llvm's cp direction              |
| address-form | a declaration or C idiom: an address taken as `lda` of a symbol (an object) where the ROM loads the same number as an immediate (`ld xrr, N`: an integer constant cast to a pointer), or back     |
| size         | C types: the same operation on a part of the same register (l / hl / xhl): a char vs int vs long variable, argument, return value or constant                                                     |
| return-form  | an option set or the C's return path: `ret cc` vs a branch to the common return, and a tail jump vs call + ret (the -O level decides both; -Xr without -O keeps one exit)                         |
| bool-form    | C idiom or option set: a truth value as `scc` vs branches loading 0 / 1 (the -O level, or `return x != 0` vs if / else)                                                                           |
| bit-form     | C idiom or option set: one bit set / cleared as `set n` / `res n` vs `or` / `and` with a mask (`x |= 8` vs a bit-field, or the -O level)                                                          |
| arith-type   | C types: a multiply or divide signed vs unsigned (mul / muls, div / divs) or byte vs word sized: the operands' declared types (char / int, signed / unsigned)                                     |
| staging      | C idiom or option set: a value stored straight to memory (`ld (mem), N`, memory to memory) vs through a register (`ld r, N` then `ld (mem), r`); the -O level and whether the value is used again |
| idiom        | option set or C: an equivalent one-instruction idiom (`ld r, 0` vs `xor r, r`, `sla r, 1` vs `add r, r`, often with a char / int size difference: then a C type too)                              |
| encoding     | a translator rule: the same instruction, another encoding (`(xsp)` vs `(xsp+0:8)`, a long vs compact immediate); asm900's choice should be taught to to_llvm                                      |
| length-only  | the C ends early or goes on: a missing or extra tail (a shared return path, a fall-through into the next routine), or the ROM size heuristic overshot                                             |
| other        | read the function: different instructions or control flow                                                                                                                                         |
